summary: Two 1930s lookout sites near Lake Coeur d'Alene; the 1934 L-4 tower was destroyed in 1957, and its footings remain, about 5.5 miles from the trailhead.

facts.design: L-4 tower, about 40 ft, with a 50-ft platform at a patrol point
facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1957; footings and a post are reported at the sites.

access.note: On national forest land; hikers reach it on foot, and some forest roads are gated.

visit.trail_note: About 5.5 miles from the Mineral Ridge Trailhead

corrections.why: Firelookout.com gives the summit tower as 40 feet; 50 feet is the patrol-point platform.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com puts the 1934 tower on the summit; WillhiteWeb puts it at the eastern of two sites and suggests the high point between them had no observation tower.
The 50-foot figure belongs to the patrol-point platform; the summit tower was 40 feet.

notes_for_editor: The record's height of 15.2 m equals 50 ft, which matches the patrol-point platform; the summit tower is 40 ft per firelookout.com and the Idaho listing gives no tower height. Where the tower stood is disputed (summit vs eastern site). WillhiteWeb and NaughtyHiker are undated hiking accounts, so the 'today' paragraph reflects their visits, not a current survey. Access 'public' is inferred from the hiking accounts on national forest land, not stated by an agency. No new photos added: WillhiteWeb's photos have no image URLs or licence.
